title: sync stops at one refused project; later ones go stale
what: Two causes. 1) lib/relay_rules.py sync(): a refused target raises Fail and ends the loop; it should record the refusal, write the other targets, and exit non-zero with a list of the refused ones. 2) write_target() does not recognise the header "Generated by ~/principles (bin/principles sync)" as relay's own; it should treat it as relay's (the old name) or migrate it.
why: Found 24 Oct after a merge: sync refused alix (its file carries the header of relay's old name, ~/principles) and exited 1, so arsenal, testenv, cartoons, clean, kartoteka, mind, sight, glyph and noisegate were not written either, silently, on every sync since the rename. Repeats on every sync (MEDIUM by the waste principle).
failing_case: A projects.toml with targets A (file has a foreign header), then B (relay's header, stale): `relay sync` exits 1 and B is unchanged.
pass_cases: Same setup: `relay sync` writes B, leaves A untouched, exits non-zero naming A and the --adopt command. A file with the old ~/principles header is rewritten without --adopt.
